Class PropertyUtils

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.util.PropertyUtils
public final class PropertyUtils extends Object
Defines the standard MDI property keys and provides type-checked construction and retrieval helpers.

  • Method Details

    • fromKeyValues

      public static Properties fromKeyValues(Object... keyValues)
      Create a set of properties from the key values.

      null or an empty array yields an empty, valid Properties. Otherwise the arguments must be an even-length sequence of alternating keys and values. Keys for known property names (see the constants in this class) are additionally checked against their expected value type; an unrecognized key is accepted with a logged warning rather than rejected, so custom keys remain usable.

      Parameters:
      keyValues - the set of key values
      Returns:
      a set of properties
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if keyValues has an odd length, if any key is not a String, if any value is null, or if a known key's value is not an instance of its expected type

    • registerKey

      public static void registerKey(String key, Class<?> expectedType)
      Register a new key and its expected type. This allows for extensibility while maintaining some level of type safety.
      Parameters:
      key - the property key to register
      expectedType - the expected type of the value associated with this key
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the key is null/blank or expected type is null
      IllegalStateException - if the key is already registered with a different expected type

    • registerKey

      public static void registerKey(String key)
      Register a new key with an expected type of Object. This is a more permissive registration that allows any type of value for the key.
      Parameters:
      key - the property key to register
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if key is null or blank

    • registerKeyOverwrite

      public static void registerKeyOverwrite(String key, Class<?> expectedType)
      Register a new key and its expected type, allowing overwriting an existing registration. This is a more permissive registration that allows changing the expected type of an already registered key.
      Parameters:
      key - the property key to register
      expectedType - the expected type of the value associated with this key
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the key is null/blank or expected type is null
